route: Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408), Entertainment Activities stream

permit.applies: The performer applies to the Department of Home Affairs, sponsored by an approved temporary activities sponsor, or, applying from outside Australia for a stay under three months, supported by a supporter who meets the support test.
permit.first: The sponsor's or supporter's consultation with the relevant union before engaging the performer, and, for film or television, an Arts certificate from the Department of Communications and the Arts.

fees.what: Visa application charge, base application charge, first instalment, any applicant not in a class the Minister specifies (Migration Regulations Sch. 1 item 1237(2)(a)(vi))

processing.note: Home Affairs' global processing times for subclass 408, Entertainment Activities stream: 90% of applications decided in 47 days, 75% in 36, 50% in 23 (applications decided to 31 August 2026, updated 29 September 2026).

permit.union: The sponsor or supporter must consult one or more Australian unions before the application: the Musicians Union of Australia for musicians and conductors, the Australian Directors Guild for foreign screen directors, the Media Entertainment and Arts Alliance for all others.
permit.eligibility: a lead actor or major support actor in a television or film production

sources.title: Department of Home Affairs, Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408), Entertainment Activities stream (content read from the page's embedded data)
sources.said: a lead actor or major support actor in a television or film production … Your sponsor or supporter must consult with the relevant union or unions before engaging you. They must also obtain an Arts certificate from the Department of Communications and the Arts … You must consult the Musicians Union of Australia (MUA) for applications for performing musicians and conductors. … You must consult the Australian Directors Guild (ADG) for applications for foreign screen directors in film, television and digital media. … You must consult the Media Entertainment and Arts Alliance (MEAA). … The maximum stay for this visa stream is 2 years. … You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. … Visa applicants who apply from outside Australia and intend to stay less than 3 months don't need a sponsor, but must have a supporter who meets the support test. … you have given reasonable opportunity to Australian citizens or residents to take part in all levels of production

note: For a government-subsidised film or television production the Arts certificate confirms the production meets Australian content criteria; for an unsubsidised one, that Australians had reasonable opportunity to take part at all levels and that foreign investment exceeds the spend on sponsored entertainers. The stay is set by the approved activity, at most two years, and the visa can't be extended. Charges for some classes the Minister specifies are lower or nil.
